answer: Each epoch the network issues a “shale‑derived” puzzle: agents must sign a fresh quill‑style proof that solves a stochastic logic circuit seeded from the previous block’s nadir hash, forcing a unique reasoning trace. The verifier checks the proof’s validity and that its computational fingerprint differs from any prior identity, rejecting duplicates. An attacker must expend a full model inference cycle (~10 GFLOP) and lock up a staking deposit of 0.5 TOKEN per fake identity, otherwise the proof is rejected.
